briefs.headline: Commanders beat the Bengals 22-20 on a field goal as time expired, ending Cincinnati's five-game run
briefs.summary: Washington defeated Cincinnati 22-20 at Northwest Stadium in Landover on Monday night before 64,101, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. Evan McPherson's 56-yard field goal with 46 seconds left had put the Bengals ahead 20-19, but Jayden Daniels, with no timeouts, hit rookie Antonio Williams for 22 and then 42 yards to reach the Cincinnati 8, and Drew Stevens kicked a 26-yard field goal as time expired, his fifth of the night, all in the second half. Joe Burrow went 28 of 40 for 300 yards and touchdowns of 31 yards to Tee Higgins and 4 to Colbie Young; Ja'Marr Chase and Higgins combined for seven catches and 74 yards against a defense that forced checkdowns, and Chase said "They did their normal, we just didn't pick it up and execute it the right way." Daniels passed for 283 yards and led Washington with 55 rushing, and Williams had nine catches for 122. Cincinnati is 7-3 and still leads the AFC North, one game ahead of Cleveland and Pittsburgh, and hosts New Orleans on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET; Washington is 4-5-1.

briefs.headline: Spurs beat the Kings 123 to 107 without Wembanyama, Fox and Harper and stay unbeaten on the road
briefs.summary: San Antonio defeated Sacramento 123 to 107 at Golden 1 Center on Monday night before 15,301, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story, with Victor Wembanyama out with back tightness two days after his 50-point, 19-rebound game, and De'Aaron Fox (shin) and Dylan Harper (hip) also ruled out. Stephon Castle had 28 points, 11 assists and eight rebounds, Julian Champagnie made six 3-pointers for 22 points, 17 of them in a 41 to 23 second quarter that turned a 12-point Kings lead into a 60 to 51 halftime edge, and Luke Kornet had 18 points and 11 rebounds; a 21 to 5 third-quarter run, nine straight by Castle, pushed the lead to 22. The Spurs went 23 of 25 at the line to Sacramento's 9 of 14 and took 20 offensive rebounds for 26 second-chance points. Domantas Sabonis had 20 points and 12 rebounds before fouling out. San Antonio has 15 wins and three losses, level with the Lakers atop the West after Los Angeles beat Utah 109 to 94, and plays at Portland on Wednesday at 10 p.m. ET in NBA Cup group play.

briefs.headline: Marshall men's soccer beats Michigan State on penalties to reach the NCAA round of 16; Wake Forest comes to Huntington Saturday
briefs.summary: Marshall advanced past Michigan State on penalty kicks in the second round of the NCAA men's soccer tournament at DeMartin Stadium in East Lansing on Sunday after the teams went scoreless through 110 minutes, per WSAZ's report and ESPN's scoreboard, which lists the match as a 0-0 draw decided on penalties. This paper did not carry the result Monday. The two sources disagree on the shootout score, WSAZ reporting 5-4 and ESPN 5-3, so none is printed. The Herd host Wake Forest in the round of 16 at Hoops Family Field on Saturday night; WSAZ lists a 7:15 p.m. kickoff and ESPN's scoreboard 7 p.m. ET, so the time is unsettled. West Virginia's season ended the same afternoon with a 1-0 double-overtime loss to defending champion Washington at Dick Dlesk Soccer Stadium, Jake Goetting scoring the winner, per WSAZ; the Mountaineers' final record differs between WSAZ (13-3-4) and ESPN (13-4-3) and is not printed.

result.note: draw after 110 minutes; Marshall advanced on penalties

briefs.headline: West Virginia men's soccer's season ends with a 1-0 double-overtime loss in Morgantown
briefs.summary: West Virginia fell to Washington, the defending NCAA champion, 1-0 in the second round of the NCAA men's soccer tournament at Dick Dlesk Soccer Stadium on Sunday, Jake Goetting scoring in the second overtime, per WSAZ; ESPN's scoreboard lists the final as 1-0 after two overtimes. This paper did not carry the result Monday. The Mountaineers' final record differs between WSAZ (13-3-4) and ESPN (13-4-3), so it is not printed. The football team plays at No. 2 Utah on Friday at 9 p.m. ET needing a win for bowl eligibility, and the basketball team plays North Carolina in Charlotte on Friday at 7 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: USMNT pipeline: U.S. Under-23s open the 2028 Olympic cycle unbeaten in Spain under Cherundolo
briefs.summary: The U.S. Under-23 men's national team drew Scotland 1-1 on Nov. 15 and beat Ukraine 3-0 on Nov. 17 at Pinatar Arena in Spain in head coach Steve Cherundolo's first camp, held Nov. 9 to 17, U.S. Soccer said Monday. Frankie Westfield scored in the 15th minute against Scotland before Eseosa Sule equalised in the 85th; Benjamin Cremaschi (15th), David Vazquez (39th) and Marvin Dills (81st, free kick) scored against Ukraine. The federation said the pool is being built for the 2028 Los Angeles Games and listed no next fixture. The senior team's next match remains the Concacaf Nations League semifinal against Mexico in March.

briefs.headline: Brentford beat 10-man Everton 4-0 six days before Everton host Liverpool in the derby
briefs.summary: Brentford defeated Everton 4-0 at the Gtech Community Stadium on Monday before 17,168, per ESPN's match report and box score, in David Moyes' 593rd match in charge of Everton, a club record passing Harry Catterick. Keane Lewis-Potter scored twice in three minutes, in the 23rd from Jaidon Anthony's low pass and in the 25th from a set piece, both deflected; captain James Tarkowski was sent off in the 40th for a studs-up lunge on Yegor Yarmolyuk, which Moyes accepted; Vitaly Janelt's 30-yard strike in the 67th and Fabio Carvalho's stoppage-time goal off the line completed it. Brentford rise to 6th on 17 points and Everton drop to 9th on 16, a point ahead of Tottenham, who fall to 10th. Everton host Liverpool in the Merseyside derby on Sunday at 7 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Onosato's seventh title and four special prizes go up on the JSA's Kyushu interview page; Hatsu is 47 days out
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association posted its champions interview page for the November tournament in Fukuoka on Tuesday, listing yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato at 13 wins and two losses for his seventh yusho (championship), with his thanks for 15 days of support and a pledge to keep working next year. The sansho (special prizes): the shukun-sho (outstanding performance award) to sekiwake Atamifuji, 11 wins and four losses, his first; kanto-sho (fighting spirit prizes) to maegashira Kinbozan, 11 wins and four losses, his third, and Tamawashi, 10 wins and five losses, his second; and the gino-sho (technique prize) to maegashira Wakamotoharu, 13 wins and two losses, his second, for his left-hand inside grip. The same page says tickets for the January tournament go on sale Dec. 5. The Hatsu basho opens Sunday, Jan. 10, at the Kokugikan in Tokyo, 47 days from today, per the JSA schedule this paper read Monday; the English year-schedule page returned an error this morning.

briefs.headline: Avdija's 31 lead the Blazers past the 76ers 128 to 111; Lakers stay level with the Spurs
briefs.summary: Portland won 128 to 111 at Philadelphia on Monday night, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story, hitting 19 3-pointers, five of them by Deni Avdija, who had 22 points by midway through the second quarter; Donovan Clingan had 15 points and 18 rebounds, and Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday scored 18 each. It was the 76ers' fourth loss against 14 wins and came a game after Milwaukee's Tyler Herro scored 50 against them. The Lakers beat Utah 109 to 94 behind Luka Doncic's 28 points and eight assists, breaking a close game open with a 17 to 5 run to start the fourth, to stay level with San Antonio at 15 wins and three losses atop the West; Indiana ended a four-game skid 125 to 120 over Oklahoma City on Pascal Siakam's 3-pointer with 44.4 seconds left, and Kelly Oubre Jr. scored a season-high 20. Portland hosts the Spurs on Wednesday at 10 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: LAFC fall 3-2 at St. Louis City in the Western Conference first-round opener
briefs.summary: St. Louis City defeated LAFC 3-2 at Energizer Park on Monday night in Game 1 of their best-of-three MLS Cup Playoffs first-round series, per ESPN's match report, never trailing: Daniel Edelman scored in the 35th minute for the club's first lead in a postseason match, Jeon Sang-bin made it 2-0 from outside the box in the 51st off a corner, Sergi Palencia headed LAFC back to 2-1 in the 62nd, substitute Simon Becher scored with his first touch in the 78th, and Denis Bouanga converted an 85th-minute penalty for his 11th playoff goal, tying Ante Razov for fifth all time. Roman Burki, back in goal for the first time since he was hurt in the U.S. Open Cup final win over Columbus on Oct. 21, made two saves. Game 2 is Saturday at 10:30 p.m. ET at BMO Stadium in Los Angeles.

briefs.headline: Monmouth falls 85-45 at North Carolina, West Virginia's opponent in Charlotte on Friday
briefs.summary: North Carolina beat Monmouth 85-45 in Chapel Hill on Monday night, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story, Terrance Brown scoring 20 points on 8-of-14 shooting and reserve Alex Samodurov adding 10 points and 11 rebounds; Jarin Stevenson had 12 points and eight rebounds, and a 29-9 first-half run put it away. The Tar Heels are 5-1 and play West Virginia, 4-2, in the Dick Vitale Invitational at Spectrum Center in Charlotte on Friday at 7 p.m. ET. Elsewhere Monday, Kansas beat Denver 84-67, Illinois beat Winthrop 133 to 83, BYU beat Washington 83-77 and Arizona beat Colorado State 96-83; Ohio opens the Jacksonville Classic against New Mexico State today at 11 a.m. ET and Marshall hosts Prairie View A&M on Wednesday at 4 p.m. ET.

going_out.limit: Flounder, all species: unlawful to possess. Striped bass, Central Southern Management Area: unlawful to possess
going_out.item: Not closing, closed: the NCDMF table lists flounder of all species as unlawful to possess, linking the 2026 recreational flounder proclamation, and lists tarpon as unlawful to possess; its striped bass line reads unlawful to possess in the Central Southern Management Area, where Topsail sits, with note (A) covering the closed Albemarle Sound season and the Atlantic Ocean's one-fish, 28- to 31-inch slot. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, read this morning at 5:55 a.m. ET Tuesday; the page states the document is effective Nov. 1, 2026, is for general informational purposes and has no legal force, and that fishery rules are subject to change.

waters.reading: 83.8 cfs, 1.54 feet at 5:15 a.m., steady on flow against 87.0 cfs and steady on stage against 1.56 feet in the fetcher's 24-hour comparison.
waters.working: The gauge at Dyer reads 83.8 cfs and 1.54 feet, the fetcher's 24-hour comparison 87.0 cfs and 1.56 feet, so the river has shed three cfs on the day and both trends read steady: the fall of the past week has flattened out and the river is holding in the low 80s. At 84 cfs and clear it is a long-leader, small-fly problem, the fish on the pocket-water lies and the tailouts rather than the seams, and in late-November water the midday hours fish best once the sun is on it. A size 18 to 20 midge or a small Blue-winged Olive nymph under a soft indicator on a 12-foot leader through the slower pockets and the tailouts is the pattern, a stonefly nymph as the point fly in the deeper plunge pools where the larger fish hold in cold water, and a sculpin pattern swung tight to the undercut banks in the first and last hour of light. Water this thin and this clear asks for a longer cast, a finer tippet and an approach from downstream; with rain due Wednesday night the flat line is the day to fish it.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.82 feet at 5 a.m., rising against 24.53 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.8 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool with ordinary bank access, up about three tenths of a foot on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and reading rising, the second morning the upper gauge has come up after a week of falling. The wing dams and the riprap are still showing rock and the water is clear enough to fish structure rather than the slack behind it: shad are the forage, so a white or shad-pattern swimbait or a lipless crankbait worked down the face of the wing dams and along the riprap is the pattern, slowed down for water that has seen a run of cold nights, with a jig and crawfish trailer on the slack side of the lock wall for the fish holding off the current. With the pool nudging up rather than falling, the fish spread back along the length of each dam instead of bunching at the channel end, so the whole face is worth covering. The R.C. Byrd tailwater itself is not gauged; this is the pool side.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.29 feet at 5 a.m., falling against 26.61 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.3 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool, down about three tenths of a foot on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and reading falling, so the two gauges that bracket the dam have crossed this morning, the pool side coming up while the lower gauge eases. Below the dam the pattern is the structure the dam makes: skipjack and shad stack in the current below the gates, and a spoon or a heavy jig worked in the churn, or a live skipjack drifted along the current seams off the lock wall, is the hybrid and catfish setup; the riprap along the Huntington bank fishes a crawfish-colour jig on the slack side where the bank current breaks. Huntington is the downstream bracket, 30-odd river miles below the dam, not the tailwater reading, which the Corps publish and this pipeline cannot fetch.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 1:18 AM at -0.2 ft, high 7:31 AM at 4.6 ft, low 2:23 PM at 0.1 ft, high 7:51 PM at 3.3 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 11:47 PM (Mon) at -0.4 ft, high 6:27 AM at 6.1 ft, low 12:56 PM at -0.2 ft, high 6:45 PM at 4.2 ft. Water 63.3F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:36 a.m. Moon full, 100% illuminated, 14.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 7:31 AM and 7:51 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Full moon this morning, 100% and 14.5 days old, and the table shows it: the 7:31 AM high at 4.6 feet in the sound is the biggest of the fortnight, after a 1:18 AM low at -0.2, with the 2:23 PM low at 0.1 and the 7:51 PM high at 3.3; the surf's 11:47 PM low belongs to Monday night and is tagged so. The sound lags the surf by 64 minutes on the morning high, 87 on the midday low and 66 on the evening high. The morning ebb drops 4.5 feet from 7:31 to 2:23 and the afternoon flood climbs 3.2 feet to 7:51, so these are the spring tides at their peak and the hardest inlet current of the month, and the water at Beaufort read 63.3F at 5:36 a.m., up 0.9 on Monday. Beach conditions: NWS Wilmington has a Coastal Flood Advisory for Coastal Pender through 8 a.m. this morning, up to half a foot of inundation on low roads along the Intracoastal Waterway and the tidal creeks on this morning's high, and the Topsail-zone forecast is mostly cloudy, a high near 59, northeast wind 9 to 13 mph gusting to 21, then rain showers Wednesday with three quarters to an inch of rain and northeast 12 to 15 gusting to 26; NWS Newport has a Coastal Flood Watch for Coastal Onslow, which includes North Topsail Beach, for 1 to 3 feet of inundation from Wednesday evening through Thursday afternoon. So today is the window before the blow. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report, a monthly, is dated Nov. 1 and is 23 days old, so it is the month's pattern and not this morning's conditions: East Coast Sports reports the piers taking red drum over 32 inches on the north end of the island, smaller reds and the occasional trout in the sound and the focus shifting to almost exclusive trout action as the weather cools; Native Son has the 5-to-8-foot seams in the main creeks as the trout target and cut bait the best bet for the reds inside; Speckled Specialist reports live shrimp under a cork as the best approach and 3/16-ounce jig heads with a soft plastic for artificials, trout in 4 to 16 feet with 4 to 8 the most common; Carolina Flats has topwater for locating trout early, deeper holes later, and soft plastics for reds on the oyster and grass banks; Jolly Roger Pier reports scattered speckled trout, Virginia mullet and spot on the bottom at night and bluefish thick early; Surf City Pier has pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom. Tied to today's table and a sound in the low 60s: the whole morning ebb is in daylight and it is the strongest of the month, so red drum's window, the last of the fall, runs roughly 11:30 a.m. to the 2:23 low on a bottom that will drain the creek mouths hard, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges where the draining grass dumps bait, or a soft plastic on the oyster and grass banks as the water leaves them. Trout want the first of the afternoon flood once the sun has been on the flats, roughly 3 to 6 p.m., in the 4-to-8-foot creek-channel seams and along the ICWW channel edge on a 3/16-ounce jig head and a small soft plastic worked slowly, or a live shrimp under a popping cork drifted over the oyster bars at the creek mouths; the hour before the 7:51 PM high falls after dark, and the dock lights on the flood after that are the night trout water. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel on the last of the flood, 6 to 8 p.m.; with the northeast wind at 9 to 13 and the surf's 6.1-foot morning high, bluefish on a metal jig from the piers in the first light, before Wednesday's rain. Flounder are release only.
